title: Gap-junction coupling scales cell competencies into larger collective goal states

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gap-junction coupling scales cell competencies into larger collective goal states

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Basal cellular competencies were not lost in the transition to multicellularity but scaled up into collective intelligence; gap-junctional merging of intracellular milieus and other tissue-level signalling (e.g. stress propagation) share chemical engrams, erase the individuality of cells, and enlarge the memory, predictive capacity and sensory/effector radius of cell networks so they can pursue larger goal states such as anatomical targets.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Scaling up from cellular competency to collective intelligence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This promotes sharing of chemical engrams, which also help to wipe the individuality of cells, and enlarges the memory, predictive capacity, and sensory/effector radius of cellular networks, enabling them to pursue larger goal states in spaces like anatomical morphospace [14].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Scaling up from cellular competency to collective intelligence”. Scope: Multicellular tissues coupled by gap junctions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Individual consequences of coupling are measurable in public molecular and imaging studies. The full claim links these effects to collective intelligence and larger goal states, for which existing datasets provide only proxies and substantial confounding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across matched tissues with altered gap-junction coupling, quantify signal propagation distance, persistence, predictive accuracy, and recovery to an anatomical setpoint. Coupling-dependent increases, rescued by restored junctional conductance, would support scaling of network capacity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched electrophysiology and anatomical outcomes are uncommon.

Gap junctions also alter metabolism and development directly.

Memory and goal pursuit have multiple operationalizations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Blockade and dye-coupling experiments already published can speak to whether electrical coupling changes the scale of pattern, but they are scattered in papers rather than a downloadable table of memory radius against coupling. Xenbase covers gene annotations, not that functional pairing. Enlarged goal states are not distinguished from a change in physiological correlation length.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate measured gap-junction coupling, or a specific blockade, to the spatial scale of a patterning outcome and to whether a transient stimulus still alters a later regenerative choice. Pattern scale shrinking under blockade, and memory of a stimulus surviving only when coupling is intact, would support the scaling claim; pattern scale and stimulus memory unchanged by coupling would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Gap-junction blockers have off-target effects, and dye coupling is not memory or predictive capacity.

No public dataset pairs coupling strength with a later anatomical setpoint across tissues.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
